title: Finite Differences for Heat and Waves

contract.reader: An engineer or student who has read entry 1 (or knows finite-difference truncation error) and has to choose a time step and a scheme for a heat or wave simulation
contract.problem: Why an explicit scheme blows up when the step is slightly too large, why implicit schemes do not, and how to choose among FTCS, BTCS, Crank-Nicolson and leapfrog
contract.outcome: Derive a scheme's amplification factor; apply mu <= 1/2 and nu <= 1; explain stiffness, Crank-Nicolson's undamped oscillation and numerical dispersion; check a scheme's order by a refinement study
contract.contribution: Every stability limit and order is shown by a short reproducible experiment, with a worked example in physical units and a decision table
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; four scripts with real output; Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy 1928, Crank-Nicolson 1947, Lax-Richtmyer 1956, LeVeque, Morton and Mayers, Strikwerda
contract.limitations: One-dimensional model problems with Dirichlet ends; two dimensions only as stated limits; nonlinear problems, other boundary conditions and higher-order schemes out of scope

findings.location: Sections 2.1, 3.1, 1.1, 4.1 display equations (desktop-light-02, 04, 07, 08); at 360 px also Sections 2.2, 2.1, 6.1 (mobile-light-07, 08, 21)
findings.problem: Four displays are wider than the column at 1280 px and scroll without a cue: the Section 2.1 truncation-error expansion is entirely hidden, the Section 3.1 tridiagonal BTCS form is cut after (1 + 2mu, the model problem loses its initial condition and the theta-scheme its delta^2 definition; at 360 px the Section 2.2 amplification factor ends at '= 1 -'
findings.whyItMatters: The truncation terms and the tridiagonal system are the results the order statements, the Crank-Nicolson argument and the implicit-solve discussion rest on; a reader who misses the hidden scroll reads them incomplete
findings.action: Break each display over lines (aligned/gathered): truncation expansion on a second line, BTCS difference and tridiagonal forms one per line, model problem conditions on a second line, theta-scheme and delta^2 as two lines; at 360 px split the amplification factor, FTCS and leapfrog updates
findings.acceptance: At 1280 px the four displays are fully visible without sideways scrolling; at 360 px the Section 2.1 truncation terms, the Section 2.2 result 1 - 4 mu sin^2(xi/2) and the Section 3.1 tridiagonal form are visible without scrolling

findings.problem: The 'Use when' column sits under the scroll shadow at 1280 px with entries cut mid-word (six columns at the 7rem minimum cell width)
findings.whyItMatters: 'Use when' is the recommendation the section exists to give
findings.action: Reduce to five columns (merge Equation into Scheme) or move 'Use when' to second position
